update.method: OT-105.8 (Luk 14:21) read in its passage (Luk 14:12-24). 10.13 Other parties told the master's anger without its ground or end; widened with the excuses (14:18-20), the report (14:21) and the end (14:24). Luk 14:12-14 (invite the poor because they cannot repay) added to OT-105 as a verse item. Rule 77: no claim is told in the touched passage.
update.claims_changed_note: One new claim: the master's anger in Luke 14 rests on the guests' refusals and ends with them shut out.
update.not_woven_note: Luk 14:12-14 to OT-105 (the poor as seen by another).

new.text: In the parable of the banquet the master's anger rests on the invited guests' refusals, turns into a wider invitation to the poor, and ends with the refusers shut out
new.beyond_text: joins the excuses (14:18-20), the anger and its command (14:21) and the end (14:24) as one account of the anger

tellings.passage: Each party that comes into anger's verses does so in its own way
